question:
A 65-year-old male presents with a 2-month history of cough and pleuritic chest pain. He reports a 5 kg
(11 lb) weight loss over the past month and intermittent swelling of his face and arms, which worsens

when lying flat. Additionally, he has recently experienced visual disturbances. He has a 50-year
smoking history but quit last year and consumes alcohol occasionally. On physical examination, he
exhibits right-sided ptosis and miosis, along with distended veins in the neck, chest, and arms. Lung
auscultation reveals clear breath sounds bilaterally. Imaging is performed. On a CT scan, where is the
mass most likely located? Answer Choices: (A) Brain stem metastasis (B) Cervical lymph nodes (C)
Anterior mediastinum (D) Right upper lobe (E) Right lower lobe (F) Left lower lobe (G) Pleural cavity
(H) Posterior mediastinum (I) Central hilar region (J) Left upper lobe
 A. Cervical lymph nodes
B. Left upper lobe
C. Anterior mediastinum
D. Left lower lobe
E. Right upper lobe
F. Pleural cavity
G. Right lower lobe
H. Central hilar region
I. Brain stem metastasis
J. Posterior mediastinum
